blocking.description:
The caller is stuck until this is decided — the `blocks-active` arm of
the critical bar. Defaults false: an agent that does not say it is
blocked is not treated as blocked.

ActionContext.description: Free-form provenance for an action (engagement / thread — soma §8).

Amount.description:
A monetary amount for `spend` classification, in minor units of a currency
(cents for USD). Compared against founder-set soft/hard caps by the
classifier.

minor_units.description: Minor units — cents for USD, pence for GBP, etc.

CasLeaseContext.description:
Execution slot lease context provisioned by CAS (Cerebral Agent Substrate).

Coordinates execution inside a warm sandbox slot (`cas-pool`) with
compiler priority clamping (`autonice` nice 19) and prefix affinity cache hints.

autonice_clamp.description: Whether Aya eBPF priority clamping (`autonice` nice 19) is requested.

prefix_affinity_hash.description: FastCache prefix affinity hash for prompt caching.

slot_id.description: Leased warm container or slot identifier.

CustodyPayload.description:
A prompt to run under blackwall custody — the shape a caller that already
holds an instruction for an agent (cortex-worker's guard-approved action
call, a named repo task) submits to the gate. Nothing in it is executed
directly: the gated verb is running the prompt in a jail whose output
lands only on settle, so the payload carries the run's parameters and no
side-effect target of its own.

Vendor-neutral by field: `provider` names a blackwall provider kind
(`"gateway"`, `"claude"`), never an endpoint or a credential.

cas_lease.description: Warm execution slot lease context provisioned by CAS.

correlation.description:
The caller's own correlation handle (cortex's ledger job id, a ticket
identifier) — carried verbatim for the audit trail, never interpreted.

intent.description:
What the submitter says this run IS (EST-377 wire half) — the
structured human intent the deck renders so card approval is
comprehension, not only a gate. Inside the payload, so inside
[`Payload::hash`]: the summary the operator reads is the bytes the
signature binds (EST-212). Absent means the submitter declared
nothing — surfaces render that absence, never a fabrication.

project.description:
blackwall project to dispatch under; the executor's default when
absent.

prompt.description: The prompt to run. Required unless `task` names a repo task.

saga.description: Correlation context for Saga flow graph orchestration and orlog stream.

task.description:
A named task (`tasks/<name>/prompt.md` in the executing repo) to
resolve the prompt from instead. Wins over `prompt` when both are set,
matching blackwall's own precedence.

virtual_workspace.description:
Virtual workspace descriptor for branchless execution (DeltaDB CRW).
Replaces physical Git worktrees on host ceres.

EmailPayload.description: The body of an email action.

Intent.description:
Submitter-declared human intent for a custody run (EST-377). Distinct from
[`CustodyPayload::correlation`]: correlation is the caller's opaque machine
handle; intent is the human-facing triple the card renders.

Every member is optional, but a present `Intent` carrying NOTHING is
refused at submit — an empty object asserts a declaration was made while
declaring nothing, which is a lie about provenance, not a lack of one.

declared_paths.description:
The paths the submitter DECLARES the run will touch. The name carries
the claim status: declared, never verified — the deck labels it as
such, and a settled changeset whose paths fall outside this list is a
mechanical escape flag (the comparison itself is follow-up work, not
this change). Relative paths only: an absolute entry is refused at
submit (the EST-239 lesson — absolute paths are how a run escapes its
jail, and they have no business in a declaration of scope either).
`Some(vec![])` is a real statement ("declares no files"); only a
wholly-absent triple makes the `Intent` empty.

summary.description: One line in plain words: what changes, where.

MessagePayload.description:
A chat-message post on a messaging platform — the platform is named only
as a field value (CANON §1c rule 4: vendor names never appear in domain
types), the same pattern as [`TicketPayload::source`]. Platform-specific
field mapping happens at the executor boundary.

Deliberately excludes anything credential- or identity-shaped (bot token,
workspace/app id, display-name/avatar customization) — that is custody's
job (the per-call lease) or fixed app configuration, never a per-action
wire field. The executor posts as the plane's own identity under the
narrowest write scope its platform offers, never a spoofed one.

Rich interactive content (block/attachment structures) is deferred BY
DESIGN, not omission: interactive elements open an inbound interaction
surface (the platform posts back on click) that the threat model does not
cover — adding it is a governance question, not a field addition.

channel.description:
Channel/conversation ID — IDs, not names: name resolution is
ambiguous across renames and needs broader read scope than this
design grants.

raw_text.description:
Disable platform markup parsing of `text` (platform default is
enabled). Set only when the gated action needs literal text.

reply_broadcast.description:
Broadcast a thread reply to the channel too. Only meaningful with
`thread` set; platform default is false.

text.description:
Message body — stays required even if rich content lands later (it is
the notification-fallback and accessibility surface).

thread.description:
Parent message id — post as a threaded reply. Maps to the platform's
native thread reference at the executor boundary.

unfurl_links.description:
Explicitly enable/disable link unfurling — the platform default
varies; set when the action cares.

Payload.description:
The off-wire payload an [`crate::wire::Action`] carries.

Serializes externally tagged, lowercase (`{"email": {"to": …}}`,
`{"ticket": {"identifier": …}}`, `{"message": {"channel": …}}`,
`{"custody": {"prompt": …}}`).

oneOf.description:
A gated chat-message post (vendor-neutral rework, 2026-08-07 jury
adjudication, of the shape ratified the same day; the executor is
the next bite).

A prompt to run under custody (governed dispatch, 2026-08-25): the
shape cortex-worker submits through the gate instead of dispatching
to blackwall directly.

RecipientClass.description:
A recipient classification a policy can gate `send-external` on
(`spend(<$500, known-vendor)`, soma §5.1; `"known-counterparty"`, §8).

The taxonomy is closed on purpose: an unrecognized recipient class fails to
deserialize rather than silently classifying as benign.

oneOf.description: Inside the org — internal writes, colleagues.
A vendor already on the books.
A counterparty in an existing engagement (soma §8 example).
No prior relationship — the most conservative outbound class.

SagaContext.description:
Correlation context for Saga flow graph orchestration.

Binds an action to a multi-repo Raid workflow DAG and its append-only
event journal (`orlog` spec 0018).

compensation_flow.description: Compensation flow identifier if the step requires rollback.

flow_node_id.description: Identifier of the specific node within the flow DAG.

orlog_stream_id.description: Append-only event stream identifier in orlog.

raid_id.description: Identifier of the overarching raid or workflow run.

TicketPayload.description:
A first-class work-item payload (EST-80) — what the soma-operator's
WorkSource funnel submits, previously shape-abused into [`EmailPayload`]
(identifier in the subject, description+URL in the body).

Verb.description:
The starter verb taxonomy for instance #0 (soma §5.1).

Serializes kebab-case to match the wire (`file-internal`, `send-external`,
`hire-engage`, `grant-access`, `delete-destroy`, `commit-code`).

oneOf.description: Delegated to terrarium's existing commit gates (soma §5.1).

VerbParams.description:
Parameters a verb carries that policies gate on (soma §5.1: "amount,
recipient class, visibility"). Every field is optional — a `read` carries
none, a `spend` carries an `amount`, a `send-external` a `recipient_class`.

`None` fields are omitted from the wire (`skip_serializing_if`) so the
serialized `params` object stays as tight as the §8 examples.

target.description:
The resource acted on, as the submitter declares it. reflexd seals an
action whose target names its own policy or state as NEVER
(`reflex::classifier::ProtectedTargets`, EST-459). Self-declared, so
that rule is a second line: it stops an honest or mistaken agent, and
the structural barriers are elsewhere (EST-460).

visibility.description: For `publish` — how widely it is exposed.

VirtualWorkspace.description:
A virtual workspace descriptor for branchless execution (DeltaDB CRW).

Replaces physical Git worktrees on disk (`git worktree add`) with an
in-memory conflict-free replicated worktree stream.

base_revision.description: Base commit SHA or snapshot revision.

delta_channel.description: Channel or endpoint for operation deltas (`(run_hash, seq)`).

thread_id.description: Thread or worktree ID in DeltaDB.

Visibility.description: Payload visibility a policy can gate `publish` on (soma §5.1).
